OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: "(?s).*\\S.*"
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: "(?s).*\\S.*"
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create/update it is
            normalized to E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a
            leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise country
            code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the
            national digits. The result must have 8 to 15 digits after the '+', and
            that E.164 string is the stored/returned value (e.g. '0412 345 678'
            becomes '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be
            a syntactically valid address. It is normalized to lower-case, and the
            stored/returned value is that lower-cased string.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered. Optional on create; when omitted
            it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO
            'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'

          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allows creating this owner even if another owner already
            has the same last name and address (i.e. they share a household).
            Optional; defaults to false.
          type: boolean
          example: false

## Summary

I implemented the business-day rule for the effective registration date in `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` (`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`):

1. **New helper `toBusinessDay(LocalDate)`** — rolls a Saturday or Sunday forward to the following Monday; weekday dates pass through unchanged.

2. **Effective date + adjustment** — the effective date is the supplied `registrationDate` if present, otherwise the server date (`LocalDate.now()`). It is then rolled to a business day, and *that adjusted value is what gets stored* on the owner. This means:
   - A supplied weekend date is now rolled forward too (behaviour change), not just the defaulted one.
   - The membership number's year segment (derived in `OwnerMapper.formatMembershipNumber` from the stored `registrationDate`) automatically uses the adjusted date — no change needed there.

3. **Daily create-limit counts per adjusted business day** — the ≥100 check now compares the new owner's adjusted date against existing owners' registration dates *also mapped through `toBusinessDay`*, so owners are grouped by business day rather than raw date. This keeps the existing daily-limit tests green even when the suite runs on a weekend (today is Saturday 2026-08-08): the seeded weekend-dated owners and the new owner both resolve to the same Monday.

The `AcceptanceTest.coreDefaultDateIsBusinessDay` invariant (default registration date is never Sat/Sun) and both V1 daily-limit tests pass, along with the full 260-test suite. Per the given spec I scoped the roll to weekends only (the acceptance base's holiday table isn't asserted by any test and isn't part of this change's spec).
